claim: Constraints on the order in which mutations accumulate are known from cancer drug treatment.

evidence: This claim is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Order constraints for species invasions are important in ecology.

claim: Order perturbations beyond sign epistasis are prevalent in the antimalarial drug-resistance landscape.
source: We apply our results to malaria parasites and find that order perturbations beyond sign epistasis are prevalent in the antimalarial drug-resistance landscape.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of malaria parasite data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The finding that order perturbations beyond sign epistasis are prevalent agrees with the observation that reversed evolution back to the ancestral type is difficult.
source: This finding agrees with the observation that reversed evolution back to the ancestral type is difficult.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the authors' findings to previously observed phenomena.

claim: Fitness landscapes were introduced by Wright in 1932.
source: The impact of suboptimal peaks has been discussed ever since fitness landscapes were introduced (Wright, 1932).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wright, 1932.

claim: A major advantage with rank orders, as compared to other statistics for fitness landscape, is that order data is robust for variation in experimental methods and measurements.
source: A major advantage with rank orders, as compared to other statistics for fitness landscape, is that order data is robust for variation in experimental methods and measurements.
evidence: This is presented as an established property of rank orders based on knowledge of their characteristics.

claim: The concept of sign epistasis was introduced by Weinreich et al. (2005).
source: The concept of sign epistasis introduced by Weinreich et al. (2005), has been important for recent work on rank orders in evolutionary biology (Kaznatcheev, 2019; Crona et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2016; de Visser and Krug, 2014; Crona et al., 2013; Poelwijk et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Weinreich et al., 2005.

claim: A system has sign epistasis if the sign of the effect of a mutation, whether positive or negative, depends on genetic background.
source: A system has sign epistasis if the sign of the effect of a mutation, whether positive or negative, depends on genetic background.
evidence: This is a definition of sign epistasis based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: All multi-peaked fitness landscapes have reciprocal sign epistasis.
source: For instance, all multi-peaked fitness landscapes have reciprocal sign epistasis (Poelwijk et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Poelwijk et al., 2011.

claim: If subsystems of type C exist, but no systems of type B, then the landscape is multi-peaked.
source: Conversely, if subsystems of type C exist, but no systems of type B, then the landscape is multi-peaked (Crona et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Crona et al., 2013.

claim: The drug-free environment had about twice as many perturbations of size 2 and 3 as the drug-exposed environment for malaria parasites.
source: However, the drug-free environment had about twice as many perturbations of size 2 and 3, as the drug-exposed environment.
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in Table 1.

claim: Sign epistasis was equally frequent in both drug-exposed and drug-free malaria fitness landscapes.
source: Sign epistasis was equally frequent in both fitness landscapes.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1 showing 55 and 54 perturbations of size 1.

claim: The summary statistic indicates that adaptation is more difficult in the drug-free environment, because few replacements of pieces of code (regardless of size) are universally beneficial.
source: The summary statistic indicates that (Table 1) adaptation is more difficult in the drug-free environment, because few replacements of pieces of code (regardless of size) are universally beneficial.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data presented in Table 1.

claim: The finding that adaptation is more difficult in the drug-free environment agrees well with the authors' observation that resistance development is a relatively straightforward process, whereas reversed evolution from the mutant 1111 back to the ancestral type is difficult.
source: This finding agrees well with the authors' observation that resistance development is a relatively straightforward process, whereas reversed evolution from the mutant 1111 back to the ancestral type is difficult.
evidence: This connects the current findings to observations from the original study by Ogbunugafor and Hartl, 2016.

claim: The complete statistics of order perturbations was better able to distinguish the landscapes than sign epistasis alone.
source: Interestingly, the complete statistics of order perturbations was better able to distinguish the landscapes than sign epistasis alone.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the discriminatory power of different analytical approaches on the data.

claim: The fitness landscape of Methylobacterium extorquens adapting to methanol does not have sign epistasis.
source: The fitness landscape does not have sign epistasis.
evidence: This is supported by the analysis of data from Chou et al., 2011, as shown in Table 2.

claim: The Methylobacterium extorquens system has size 2 perturbations.
source: However, the system has size 2 perturbations (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data analysis presented in Table 2.

claim: The perturbations in Methylobacterium extorquens show that the rank order is incompatible with additive fitness.
source: The perturbations show that the rank order is incompatible with additive fitness.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of size 2 perturbations.

claim: For additive fitness where all mutations decrease fitness, the proportion of unexpected results (increased fitness) decreases by the number of loci replaced.
source: In both cases, the proportion of unexpected results decreases by the number of loci replaced.
evidence: This is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 3.

claim: The reason that the proportion of unexpected results decreases with more loci replaced is that the noise level is similar in all cases, whereas the effect size is not.
source: The reason is that the noise level is similar in all cases, whereas the effect size is not.
evidence: This is an inference explaining the pattern observed in the simulations.

claim: Constraints on the orders in which mutation occur are known for development of cancer drug resistance.
source: Constraints on the orders in which mutation occur are known for development of cancer drug resistance (Hosseini et al., 2019; Beerenwinkel et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hosseini et al., 2019 and Beerenwinkel et al., 2007a.

claim: Exactly 384 orders are compatible with the absence of sign epistasis for n=3.
source: As remarked in Crona et al. (2017), exactly 384 orders are compatible with the absence of sign epistasis for n=3.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Crona et al., 2017.

claim: Exactly 96 out of the 384 orders compatible with absence of sign epistasis are compatible with additive fitness for n=3.
source: By applying order perturbations (and by inspection), we verified that exactly 96 out of the 384 orders are compatible with additive fitness
evidence: This is based on the authors' computational verification.

claim: Only 0.24 percent of all 40,320 rank orders for three-locus systems are compatible with additive fitness.
source: or 0.24 percent of all 40,320 rank orders for three-locus systems.
evidence: This is calculated from the data that 96 out of 40,320 orders are compatible with additive fitness.

claim: It is straightforward to verify that a rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless it has rectangular perturbations for n=4.
source: It is straightforward to verify that a rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless it has rectangular perturbations for n=4.
evidence: This is stated as a verifiable mathematical property.

claim: Counterexamples to the statement that a rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless it has rectangular perturbations exist for n=5.
source: However, counterexamples to the analogous statement for n=5 exist (Kraft et al., 1959)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kraft et al., 1959.

claim: Sign epistasis implies that a system has signed circuit interactions, but the converse is not true.
source: We have established that sign epistasis implies that a system has signed circuit interactions, but the converse is not true.
evidence: This is a logical relationship established through the authors' theoretical analysis.

claim: A rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless there is sign epistasis for a two-locus system.
source: A rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless there is sign epistasis for a two-locus system.

claim: For four-locus systems, a rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless there are rectangular perturbations.
source: For four-locus systems, a rank order is compatible with additive fitness unless there are rectangular perturbations.
evidence: This is stated as a verifiable mathematical property.

claim: Only a very small proportion of all rank orders are compatible with additive fitness.
source: In general, only a very small proportion of all rank orders are compatible with additive fitness
evidence: This is inferred from the specific calculations for n=3 and general mathematical considerations.

claim: Rectangular perturbations have the capacity to detect epistasis when conventional rank-order-based methods cannot.
source: Rectangular perturbations have the capacity to detect epistasis when conventional rank-order-based methods cannot.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Methylobacterium extorquens example where size 2 perturbations detected epistasis in the absence of sign epistasis.

claim: Rank orders are insufficient for determining the effect of genetic recombination.
source: Rank orders are insufficient for determining the effect of genetic recombination (de Visser et al., 2009; Otto and Lenormand, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Visser et al., 2009 and Otto and Lenormand, 2002.

claim: Evolutionary predictability is sensitive for population parameters.

claim: The importance of accessible mutational trajectories is not universal.

claim: All circuits are zero if fitness is additive.
